      Industrial Development Scheme for J&K

       The New Central Sector Scheme (NCSS) for Industrial Development of Jammu &
        Kashmir, launched on February 19, 2021, aims to catalyze industrial growth in the Union
         Territory (UT) by attracting investments, generating employment, and fostering socio-
       economic development. With a substantial financial outlay of ₹28,400 crore, the
       scheme is set to be implemented over a period extending up to 2036-37 .

        Objectives:

             Industrial Development: Stimulate the establishment and expansion of industries in
         Jammu & Kashmir.

          Employment Generation: Create job opportunities, thereby contributing to the
           socio-economic upliftment of the region.

        Incentives Under the Scheme:

        Capital Investment Incentive (CII):

       Zone A: 30% subsidy on investment in plant & machinery (manufacturing) or
        construction of buildings and other durable physical assets (service sector), up to a
      maximum of ₹5 crore.

       Zone B (Far-off areas): 50% subsidy on similar investments, capped at ₹7.5 crore.

        Applicable for units with an investment up to ₹50 crore.

        Capital Interest Subvention (CIS):

Interest subvention at an annual rate of 6% for a maximum of 7 years on loan amounts
       up to ₹500 crore for investment in plant & machinery (manufacturing) or construction of
         buildings and other durable physical assets (service sector).

       Goods & Services Tax Linked Incentive (GSTLI):

            Incentive equivalent to 300% of the eligible value of actual investment made in plant
         & machinery (manufacturing) or construction of buildings and other durable physical
            assets (service sector) over 10 years.

          The annual incentive amount will not exceed one-tenth of the total eligible incentive.

       Working Capital Interest Subvention (WCIS):

         Interest subvention at an annual rate of 5% for a maximum of 5 years on working capital
         loans, with a maximum limit of ₹1 crore.

    Make in India

       The Make in India initiative, launched on September 25, 2014, by Prime Minister
        Narendra Modi, aims to transform India into a global manufacturing and design hub. It
       encourages both domestic and international companies to manufacture their products in
          India, thereby boosting employment, enhancing skill development, and increasing the
        manufacturing sector's contribution to the GDP.

        Objectives:

          Encourage Manufacturing: Promote companies to manufacture their products
             within India.

           Transform India into a Global Hub: Develop India as a global center for design and
            manufacturing.

          Job Creation and Skill Enhancement: Generate employment opportunities and
          enhance skill development.

        Four Pillars of Make in India:

          1. New Processes: Simplify and rationalize existing rules and procedures, making them
          more transparent and business-friendly.

          2. New Infrastructure: Develop state-of-the-art infrastructure and industrial corridors
             to facilitate investment.

          3. New Sectors: Open up various sectors for foreign direct investment (FDI), including
           defense production, insurance, and medical devices.

          4. New Mindset: Shift the government's role from a regulator to a facilitator, creating a
           conducive environment for business.

        Sectors Covered:

Under Make in India 2.0, the initiative focuses on 27 sectors, comprising 15

     Remission of Duties & Taxes on Exported Products

       The Remission of Duties and Taxes on Exported Products (RoDTEP) Scheme is a
         flagship initiative by the Government of India, launched on January 1, 2021, to enhance
        the competitiveness of Indian exports by reimbursing embedded taxes and duties that
        are not refunded through other mechanisms.

        Objectives:

           Boost Exports: Reduce the cost of exports by refunding unrebated taxes and duties.

       WTO Compliance: Replace the Merchandise Exports from India Scheme (MEIS) to
             align with World Trade Organization (WTO) norms.

            Simplify Refund Process: Provide an automatic and digitized route for refunding
             input taxes and duties.

       Key Features:

       Scope: Applies to all sectors, with priority given to labor-intensive industries.

          Eligibility:

         No minimum turnover requirement.

          Goods exported through e-commerce platforms are eligible.

           Country of origin must be India; re-exported goods are excluded.

       Refund Mechanism: Rebates are provided as a percentage of the Freight On Board
        (FOB) value, with rates and value caps notified by the government.

         Digital Implementation: The scheme is implemented through an end-to-end IT system,
        ensuring seamless processing and monitoring.

        Administrative Framework:

           Coordinating Agency: The scheme is administered by the Department of Revenue,
             Ministry of Finance, in coordination with the Department of Commerce, Ministry of
         Commerce and Industry.

         RoDTEP Committee: A committee has been constituted to review and recommend
              ceiling rates under the scheme for different export sectors. The committee interacts
            with Export Promotion Councils and Chambers of Commerce to discuss
           methodologies and implementation issues.

      Start-up India Seed Fund Scheme

       The Startup India Seed Fund Scheme (SISFS), launched in April 2021 by the
       Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), aims to provide





GOVERNMENT SCHEMES (Part-2)                                                                                         6

financial assistance to startups for proof of concept, prototype development, product
           trials, market entry, and commercialization.

        Duration: 4 years (2021–2025)

         Total Corpus: ₹945 crore

        Target: Support approximately 3,600 startups through 300 incubators

       Nodal Department: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT)

          Eligibility Criteria:

        For Startups:

          Must be recognized by DPIIT and incorporated not more than 2 years prior to
             application.

           Should not have received more than ₹10 lakh of monetary support under any other
            Central or State Government scheme.

           Shareholding by Indian promoters should be at least 51% at the time of application.

           Should have a business idea to develop a product or service with a market fit, viable
            commercialization, and scope of scaling.

        For Incubators:

          Must be a legal entity: a society registered under the Societies Registration Act 1860,
           a trust registered under the Indian Trusts Act 1882, a private limited company
            registered under the Companies Act 1956 or the Companies Act 2013, or a statutory
          body created through an Act of the legislature.

           Should be operational for at least two years on the date of application.

          Must have facilities to seat at least 25 individuals.

           Should have at least 5 startups undergoing incubation physically on the date of
             application.

          Must have a full-time Chief Executive Officer, experienced in business development
          and entrepreneurship, supported by a capable team responsible for mentoring
            startups in testing and validating ideas, as well as in finance, legal, and human
           resources functions.

       Funding Structure:

        For Incubators: Grants of up to ₹5 crore to eligible incubators selected by the Experts
        Advisory Committee (EAC).

        For Startups:

         Up to ₹20 lakh for validation of Proof of Concept, prototype development, or product
                trials.

Up to ₹50 lakh for market entry, commercialization, or scaling up through convertible

      e-Biz portal

       The e-Biz Portal was India's pioneering Government-to-Business (G2B) platform,
        launched on January 28, 2013, by the Department of Industrial Policy and Promotion
         (DIPP), now known as the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade
         (DPIIT). Developed by Infosys Technologies Limited under a 10-year Public-Private
        Partnership (PPP) model, the portal aimed to streamline and digitize business-related
        services across various government departments.

        Objectives:

          Single-Window Access: Provide a 24x7 online single-window system for efficient
          and convenient G2B services to investors and businesses.

            Lifecycle Support: Offer services throughout the business lifecycle, including
            planning, starting, operating, and closing a business.

          Reduce Complexity: Minimize the complexity in obtaining information and services
             related to starting and operating businesses in India.

          Enhance Transparency: Improve transparency and efficiency in the delivery of
           government services to the business community.

       Key Features:

          Comprehensive Services: The portal provided a one-stop shop for obtaining
            information and forms; submission of forms/applications; online payment and
             routing of fees; and routing of forms/applications and fees to various departments
              for licenses, permits, registrations, approvals, clearances, permissions, periodic
               filings, and compliances throughout the lifecycle of a business entity.

            Integrated Payment Gateway: Facilitated online payments for various services
           through an integrated payment system.

          Customized Information: Allowed business users to obtain a customized list of
             licenses, permits, and regulations required across all levels of government.

              Pilot Implementation: Initially launched in five pilot states: Andhra Pradesh, Delhi,
           Haryana, Maharashtra, and Tamil Nadu.

        Implementation Phases:

          Pilot Phase (First 3 Years):

         Integration of 29 services in the first year and 21 services in the subsequent two years,
         including 26 services of Central Government departments and 24 services in each of
        the 5 pilot states.

       Expansion Phase (Next 7 Years):

Planned to cover over 200 services across the country, expanding the reach and

      Niryat Bandhu Scheme

       The Niryat Bandhu Scheme is a flagship initiative launched by the Directorate General
        of Foreign Trade (DGFT) under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of
          India, on 13th October 2011. The scheme aims to mentor new and potential exporters,
         especially first-generation entrepreneurs and Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises
       (MSMEs), by providing them with the necessary guidance and knowledge to engage in
         international trade.

        Objectives:

           Mentorship: To reach out to new and potential exporters and mentor them through
             orientation programmes, counselling sessions, and individual facilitation on various
           aspects of foreign trade.

           Capacity Building: To build the capacity of first-time exporters to enable them to
           conduct business legally and efficiently.

           Export Promotion: To boost exports from India by facilitating the entry of new
            entrepreneurs into international trade.

       Implementing Agency:

       The scheme is implemented by the Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT). Under
          this scheme, officers of DGFT, designated as 'Niryat Bandhu' (meaning 'Export Friend'),
       assume the role of mentors for interested individuals.

       Key Features:

            Training and Seminars: Regular training sessions and seminars are conducted for
         new Importer Exporter Code (IEC) holders and potential exporters to educate them
           about the intricacies of foreign trade.

          Focus on MSME Clusters: The scheme targets MSME clusters identified by DGFT
              for imparting training and seminars regarding issues of international trade.

            Collaboration with Institutions: Seminars are also conducted at industry
             associations, management schools, universities, and other institutions to reach a
           wider audience.

        Niryat Bandhu @ Your Desktop

          In September 2015, DGFT, in collaboration with the Indian Institute of Foreign Trade
          (IIFT), launched 'Niryat Bandhu @ Your Desktop', an online certificate program in
        export-import business.

       Program Details:

            Duration: 20 live sessions conducted over five days a week from 6 PM to 8 PM IST.

Batch Size: Each batch accommodates up to 60 participants.

        Curriculum: The program covers various topics, including:

             Introduction to Export/Import and assessing export readiness.

           Understanding international markets and trade opportunities.

            Regulatory documents involved in foreign trade.

          Customs clearance procedures.

           Duty Drawback schemes and claim procedures.

            Incorporating INCOTERMS in sales contracts.

            Export finance and payment mechanisms.

           Currency risk management.

             Logistics and supply chain management.

         Certification: Upon successful completion, participants receive a certificate jointly
       awarded by DGFT and IIFT.

     Government e-Marketplace

       The Government e-Marketplace (GeM) is a transformative initiative by the Government
         of India, launched on August 9, 2016, by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry. It
        serves as a one-stop, online platform for public procurement, facilitating the acquisition
         of goods and services by various government departments, organizations, and public
        sector undertakings (PSUs) .

        Objectives:

           Streamline Procurement: Simplify and digitize the procurement process to make it
          more efficient and transparent.

          Enhance Transparency: Reduce human intervention to minimize corruption and
           ensure fair practices.

          Promote Inclusivity: Encourage participation from Micro, Small, and Medium
            Enterprises (MSMEs), startups, women entrepreneurs, and artisans.

       Key Features:

          Comprehensive Procurement Tools: Offers e-bidding, reverse e-auction, and
         demand aggregation to facilitate competitive pricing.

            User-Friendly Interface: Provides a dynamic, self-sustaining, and user-friendly
             portal for government buyers and sellers.

          Mandatory Usage: As per Rule 149 of the General Financial Rules (GFR) 2017,
           procurement of goods and services by government users through GeM is mandatory
                     .

Cost Savings: An independent assessment by the World Bank indicated average
            savings of about 9.75% on median prices for buyers using GeM.

        Evolution to GeM 3.0;

          In response to technological advancements and stakeholder feedback, GeM 3.0 was
        launched on January 26, 2018. This version introduced several enhancements:

           Standardized Catalogue Management: Ensures uniformity in product and service
               listings.

          Advanced Search Engine: Facilitates real-time price comparisons using third-party
              sites.

         e-EMD and e-PBG: Introduced electronic Earnest Money Deposit and Performance
          Bank Guarantee mechanisms.

          Performance-Based User Rating: Implements a rating system based on user
           performance.

           Online Vendor Assessment: Optional feature for evaluating vendors.

          Market-Based Bundling: Allows bundling and bunching of products and services.

            Multi-Cart Functionality: Enables users to manage multiple carts simultaneously.

          Expanded Services: Offers more services with Bid and Reverse Auction facilities

    GeM SAHAY’ app

       The GeM SAHAY initiative is a digital lending platform launched by the Government e-
        Marketplace (GeM) under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry. It aims to provide
        Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) with instant, collateral-free loans to
             fulfill government purchase orders, thereby addressing the working capital challenges
        faced by these enterprises.

       Launch Date: June 2021

        Purpose: To facilitate quick and easy access to credit for MSMEs against confirmed
        purchase orders on the GeM platform.

       Implementing Agency: GeM, in collaboration with the Indian Software Product Industry
       Round Table (iSPIRT), a non-profit tech think tank.

       Key Features:

            Instant Loan Disbursement: Loans are disbursed instantly upon acceptance of a
           purchase order on the GeM platform.

            Collateral-Free Financing: MSMEs can avail of loans without the need for any
              collateral.

             Digital Process: The entire loan application and disbursement process is digital,
            ensuring ease and transparency.

Loan Amount: Up to ₹10 lakh, with a minimum of 80% of the purchase order value.

          Loan Tenure: Typically ranges from 60 to 120 days.

             Interest Rates: Competitive rates, varying based on the lender and borrower's credit
              profile.

          Eligibility Criteria:

        GeM Registration: The applicant must be a registered seller on the GeM platform.

           Business Type: Initially targeted sole proprietors; however, with the introduction of
        GeM SAHAY 2.0, all sellers, including partnerships and companies, are eligible.

          Purchase Orders: Must have confirmed purchase orders with payment types such
           as PFMS, GeM Pool, or CRPF Online account.

         Udyam Registration: For non-existing customers of participating banks, an Udyam
             Certificate issued by the Ministry of MSME is required

     GeM SAHAY 2.0

              In response to the evolving needs of MSMEs, GeM introduced SAHAY 2.0, which
              offers:

          Expanded Eligibility: Extends loan facilities to all types of sellers, beyond sole
             proprietors.

            Faster Processing: Loan approvals within 10 minutes.

          Enhanced Technology: Built on the Open Credit Enablement Network (OCEN)
           framework, ensuring seamless integration between lenders and borrowers

      Start-ups Intellectual Property Protection Scheme

       The Start-ups Intellectual Property Protection (SIPP) Scheme is a flagship initiative by
        the Government of India, launched in 2016, to encourage innovation and facilitate the
         protection of Intellectual Property Rights (IPRs) among startups. Implemented by the
        Office of the Controller General of Patents, Designs & Trademarks (CGPDTM) under
        the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of
      Commerce and Industry, the scheme aims to provide startups with access to high-
         quality IP services and resources.

        Objectives:

          Promote Awareness: Educate startups about the importance of IPRs and the
            benefits of protecting them.

             Facilitate IP Protection: Assist startups in filing and processing patent, design, and
           trademark applications through registered facilitators.

            Financial Support: Bear the facilitation fees for IP filings, reducing the financial
           burden on startups

Key Features:

          Empanelled Facilitators: Startups are assisted by IP facilitators (also known as "IP
             Mitras") who provide services such as drafting, filing, and responding to examination
            reports for patents, trademarks, and designs.

          Fee Rebates: Startups receive an 80% rebate on patent filing fees and a 50% rebate
          on trademark application fees.

           Fast-Track Examination: Provision for expedited examination of patent applications
               filed by startups.

          Government-Borne Facilitation Fees: The government bears the entire cost of
               facilitation services provided by the IP Mitras

      Scheme Extensions and Revisions:

              First Extension: In 2020, the scheme was extended for three years until March 31,
           2023.

          Second Extension: Further extended for another three years, effective from April 1,
           2023, until March 31, 2026.

    Scheme for Investment Promotion

       The Scheme for Investment Promotion (SIP) is a centrally sponsored initiative launched
          in November 2008 by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade
         (DPIIT) under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry. The scheme aims to attract and
          facilitate investments into India, thereby enhancing the country's global competitiveness
       and economic growth.

        Objectives:

       Promote Foreign Direct Investment (FDI): Encourage and facilitate FDI into India by
         creating a conducive investment climate.

       Enhance International Cooperation: Strengthen international partnerships and
        cooperation to promote FDI.

        Capacity Building: Develop institutional capacities to support investment promotion
          activities.





GOVERNMENT SCHEMES (Part-2)                                                                                                           13

Implementing Agency:

       Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT): The DPIIT is
        responsible for the implementation and oversight of the SIP.

         Financial Outlay:

       ₹970 Crore (2021–2026): The Central Government has approved the continuation of the
        SIP for five years, from 2021 to 2026, with a total financial outlay of ₹970 crore.

       Key Components and Activities:

           Investment Promotion: Organizing and participating in investment promotion
            events, roadshows, and exhibitions to showcase India's investment opportunities.

            Policy Advocacy: Engaging with stakeholders to identify and address policy and
            regulatory issues affecting investments.

            Investor Facilitation: Providing support and facilitation services to investors to ease
            the investment process.

          Research and Information Dissemination: Conducting research and disseminating
            information related to investment opportunities and policies.

      Indian Footwear and Leather Development Program

       The Indian Footwear and Leather Development Programme (IFLDP) is a Central Sector
       Scheme launched in 2017 by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal
        Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry. It aims to develop infrastructure for
        the leather sector, address environmental concerns, facilitate additional investments,
        generate employment, and increase production.

       Extended Phase (2021–2026)

          In January 2022, the Union Cabinet approved the continuation of IFLDP until March 31,
        2026, or until further review, with a total financial outlay of ₹1,700 crore.

       Sub-Schemes Under IFLDP:

       The extended program comprises six sub-schemes:

          1. Sustainable Technology and Environmental Promotion (STEP) – ₹500 crore

          2. Integrated Development of Leather Sector (IDLS) – ₹500 crore

          3. Establishment of Institutional Facilities – ₹200 crore

          4. Mega Leather, Footwear and Accessories Cluster Development (MLFACD) – ₹300
            crore

          5. Brand Promotion of Indian Brands in Leather and Footwear Sector – ₹100 crore

          6. Development of Design Studios – ₹100 crore

Industrial Infrastructure Upgradation Scheme

       The Industrial Infrastructure Upgradation Scheme (IIUS) was launched in 2003 by the
       Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce
       and Industry, to enhance the competitiveness of domestic industries by providing quality
         infrastructure through public-private partnerships in selected functional clusters.

        Modified Industrial Infrastructure Upgradation Scheme (MIIUS):

          In July 2013, the scheme was modified and renamed as the Modified Industrial
         Infrastructure Upgradation Scheme (MIIUS) to address implementation challenges and
        incorporate recommendations from independent evaluations.

        Objectives:

          Enhance industrial competitiveness by providing quality infrastructure.

           Support upgradation of infrastructure in existing industrial parks, estates, and areas.

           Undertake greenfield projects in backward areas, including the North Eastern Region
            (NER).

       Funding Pattern:

        General Areas:

            Central Grant: 50% of the project cost, subject to a ceiling of ₹50 crore.

            State Implementing Agency: At least 25% of the project cost.

       North Eastern and Hill States:

            Central Grant: 80% of the project cost.

            State Implementing Agency: 10% of the project cost.

          The remaining funding is to be mobilized from other stakeholders, including industry
             contributions.

        Implementation Mechanism

         Projects are implemented through Special Purpose Vehicles (SPVs) formed by the
         cluster associations.

      A Project Management Agency (PMA) assists DPIIT in appraising proposals and
        monitoring projects.

         Projects are selected based on diagnostic studies and stakeholder consultations,
        ensuring need-based interventions.

     Transport and Marketing Assistance Scheme

       The Transport and Marketing Assistance (TMA) Scheme was launched by the
       Government of India in March 2019 to provide financial assistance for the international
       component of freight and marketing of agricultural produce, thereby mitigating the





GOVERNMENT SCHEMES (Part-2)                                                                                                             15

disadvantage of higher transportation costs faced by Indian exporters of agricultural
        products.

        Timeline and Revisions:

           Initial Phase: Applicable for exports effected from March 1, 2019, to March 31, 2020.

          First Extension: Extended up to March 31, 2021.

        Revised Scheme: Applicable for exports effected from April 1, 2021, to March 31, 2022.

       Major Changes in the Revised Scheme:

        Inclusion of Dairy Products: Previously excluded, dairy products became eligible for
        assistance under the revised scheme.

        Increased Rates of Assistance:

        50% increase for exports by sea.

         100% increase for exports by air.

        Objectives:

          To provide assistance for the international component of freight and marketing of
             agricultural produce.

          To mitigate the disadvantage of higher transportation costs faced by Indian
            exporters of agricultural products.

          To promote brand recognition for Indian agricultural products in specified overseas
            markets.

          Eligibility Criteria:

           Products Covered: Specified agricultural products, including dairy, as notified by the

             agricultural laborers in the state.
